result.burst: FLIP-SPLIT: BURST=128 wins every throughput cell (c=1 +5-7%, c=8 +6.9%, 512-tok +7-8%, q9 +9.2%, byte-identical, local optimum at 128) BUT costs the streaming felt path 2.8x first-chunk latency — winner-by-context, not unconditional. Default stays 32 (latency-safe, the daily pill regime); serve configs that are throughput-tier (load-serve batch, judge/harvest lanes, c>=2) get 128 documented as the measured optimum. No code change — env stays the seam.
result.K: NO FLIP: shipped K=3 default CONFIRMED on 82 SM (K=5 loses at B32 -4.9%, and at B128 K=3 still beats K=5 by +1.9%). The pod's K=5 row is a 188-SM serving config, stays pod-scoped.
result.pmin: NO FLIP: +15-20pp acceptance reproduces (0.75->0.82 at K3, 0.73->0.87 q9) but e2e is flat-to-negative at the K=3 optimum on 82 SM. The pod's +6.1% was a K=5-chain effect. PMIN=0.3+PMIN0 stays an env door for deep-K configs.
result.sm_dependence: CONFIRMED ASYMMETRY: 82 SM optimum = K3/B128/pmin-off; 188 SM optimum = K5/B128/pmin-on. A per-SM gate (graph-key-48 precedent, decode.rs sm_count()>=180) would only matter if K/pmin defaults flipped — they don't, so no code gate needed; the pod rows remain the PRO 6000 deploy config.
